Related Article Israeli-Palestinian conflict ‘We have expressed sympathy’: Israeli ambassador declines to apologise for Zomi Frankcom killing The Israeli military said the presence of armed security to accompany the convoy “was not coordinated with IDF authorities” and the vehicles had deviated from the route arranged in advance, while several people were also mistakenly identified as armed persons. “Following review of all findings of the factual assessment, it was determined that, notwithstanding serious failures in the process that led to the assessment that Hamas operatives were travelling in the vehicles, the decisions of the commanders did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct,” the IDF said. It added that there was “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation”.



Two Israeli officers were dismissed from their positions and three senior officers were formally reprimanded, according to the Israeli military. WCK said it fundamentally disagreed with the decision not to pursue a criminal investigation. “We strongly condemn the Israeli military prosecutor’s account of the deaths of our seven colleagues on April 1, 2024,” the aid organisation said in a statement. “There has never been any excuse or justification for the attacks, and there is nothing in this account that does so. The decision is inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive.” Wong spoke in Canberra on Wednesday at a Parliament House event attended by Frankcom’s family to launch the Zomi Frankcom Humanitarian Award.



“Two years on from Zomi Frankcom’s death, the pain of her loss remains with us,” she said. “People like Zomi are rare, and their courage deserves to be celebrated. “I want to make it clear that the Australian government continues to press the Israeli government for full accountability for the deaths of Zomi and her World Central Kitchen colleagues. Zomi and her family deserve justice.” Foreign Minister Penny Wong with Zomi Frankcom’s brother, Mal Frankcom, in September 2025. Dominic Lorrimer In a report released in July 2024, former Australian Defence Force chief Mark Binskin found that “a significant breakdown in situational awareness” by the Israeli military caused the strike that killed Frankcom, adding he did not believe the charity workers were deliberately targeted.



The IDF said its Fact-Finding and Assessment Mechanism (FFAM) had reviewed approximately 150 incidents since the beginning of the war, then transferred them for examination by the Military Prosecution. Related Article Israeli-Palestinian conflict Netanyahu bluntly rejects Trump’s Gaza plan to disarm Hamas Rajab and her family were trapped in a vehicle under fire in Gaza City in January 2024, while she pleaded for help by phone with her cousin Layan Hamada beside her. The IDF concluded that in the hours shortly after the firing, following a telephone call to rescue authorities, the movement of a Palestine Red Crescent ambulance was coordinated for the purpose of evacuating the casualties. “However, according to the allegations raised, upon the ambulance’s arrival at the scene of the incident, a shell was fired toward it, resulting in the deaths of the two paramedics travelling in it,” the IDF said.



“Several days later, the bodies of the seven members of the Hamada family, including the bodies of Hind and Layan, were recovered from the vehicle. In addition, the bodies of the two paramedics were recovered from the ambulance. “It has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division (MPCID). In light of this decision, no further details can be provided beyond the above with respect to the aspects arising from the FFAM’s review.” The 15 Palestinian paramedics were killed as they drove in the southern city of Rafah in March 2025. The IDF decided not to take criminal action over the killings of four staffers from Doctors Without Borders in two separate instances in November 2023 and February 2024. On Wednesday, an Israeli airstrike killed nine Palestinians at a police station in Gaza, medics said.



Medics and police sources said several officers were among those killed at what the Hamas-led interior ministry said was the headquarters of the municipal police. Fifteen others were wounded. The Israeli military said it had struck Hamas militants who “operated from the civilian police station” to advance attacks against its troops. With Reuters Get a note directly from our foreign correspondents on what’s making headlines around the world.

World.title: Alan Jones trial live updates: ‘Complainant C’ cross-examination to continue after text messages showing rift between former 2GB radio figures revealed
World.content:
Warning: Graphic content

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of day 12 of Alan Jones’ criminal trial on charges of indecent assault and sexual touching. My colleague Clare Sibthorpe will be bringing you the latest from the courtroom today.

The NSW Local Court in Sydney’s historic Downing Centre court building will hear further evidence today from complainant “C”, the second of six men who have accused the former 2GB host of unwanted touching and kissing over a 20-year period.

Alan Jones arrives at the Downing Centre Local Court on Wednesday. Peter Rae

Jones denies the claims and is entitled to the presumption of innocence.

Jones is charged with indecently assaulting “C” eight times over a five-month period by touching and kissing him without his consent. The alleged incidents are said to have taken place almost 20 years ago.

“C”, a former staffer to Jones, faces further cross-examination today by Jones’ barrister, Gabrielle Bashir, SC, after the questioning was cut short on Wednesday afternoon by legal argument.

The Crown alleges that Jones indecently assaulted or sexually touched six men without their consent between 2003 and 2020, and is seeking to prove 22 charges against him.

Bashir said during her opening address to the court that the credibility and reliability of the complainants’ evidence would be tested.

Support is available from the National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service at 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732) or the Men’s Referral Service on 1300 766 491.

World.title: Souths make call on Latrell Mitchell’s return with comeback plan
World.content:
Latrell Mitchell’s long-awaited return for the Rabbitohs has been delayed for another week, but South Sydney’s highest-paid player is closing in on a comeback and much-needed game time leading into the finals. Coach Wayne Bennett had raised hopes of Mitchell playing his first game since round 10 when he was included in the Rabbitohs extended squad for Saturday’s clash against the Warriors, with Bennett telling this masthead Mitchell was “a chance” if he could complete full training this week. Latrell Mitchell at South Sydney training earlier this week. Steven Siewert But Souths have opted to keep their superstar centre on ice for another week. They also confirmed there have been no setbacks in his recovery from an ongoing nerve issue in his lower back. The nerve damage was linked to subsequent upper leg and calf problems for Mitchell which ruled him out of NSW’s Origin campaign. The Rabbitohs have targeted next week’s round 26 match against the Titans for Mitchell to return to the paddock, though that is still contingent on him handling increased training loads.



Bennett has flagged a potential bench role for Mitchell, who is unlikely to be played for a full 80 minutes against either the Gold Coast or arch-rivals the Roosters in the final round of the regular season. ‘I wish I got injured instead of him’: Brotherly love ahead of Trbojevic comeback Adrian Proszenko Jake Trbojevic has paid tribute to brother Tom as he embarks on another comeback, saying most players in his position would have written off the year. Tom Trbojevic is a huge addition to a Manly side that remains a mathematical possibility of squeaking into the finals if they beat Newcastle at McDonald Jones Stadium on Saturday.



The Sea Eagles haven’t won a game since their captain suffered his latest hamstring injury, in round 20. However, the fullback will be a welcome addition to a side that has lost halfback Joey Walsh to a fractured jaw. Another Trbojevic, youngest sibling Ben, also returns from injury. “I’ll be honest, it is tough, it’s really tough,” Jake Trbojevic said about playing without Tom. “I’ve got a lot of respect for Tom, obviously being my brother and all that, but the way he goes about things – he is a true professional. “Everyone says that about people, but he genuinely is. Sometimes I wish it was me who got injured instead of him, because he puts in 10 times more work than anyone else to get his body right, and he’s just been very unlucky.



Tom Trbojevic, Jake Trbojevic and Ben Trbojevic Getty Images “It’s very hard to see, particularly being his older brother. Not only that, selfishly I want him out on the field because he makes us better, you know? So, it is tough, but I’m happy for him that he’s very resilient and keeps working hard. These things don’t hold him back. “A lesser man would probably say, ‘You know what, I’ll just sit the year out and come back next year,’ but he’s fighting. He wants to be out there, he wants to lead this club, and that’s great.” If Tom Trbojevic’s return is successful he could put himself into contention for Australia selection for the end-of-year World Cup. Much will depend on how he and Manly perform in coming weeks, although it’s unlikely the club will feature in the post-season. “There’s always a chance,” Jake Trbojevic said. “Tom wants to play for Manly, it doesn’t matter what’s on the line, he wants to be out there. He’s the captain of this club for a reason, and we love having him out there. The Northern Beaches loves having him out there. We’re better for it.



Tom Trbojevic. Getty “So, it doesn’t matter what’s on the line—whether it’s finals or no finals—we want him out there, he wants to be out there, and he works extremely hard, so he deserves to be out there. We’re going to go out there, put in a great performance, and he’s going to lead us well. Hopefully, we can keep improving and turn this around.” Manly winger Jason Saab said Tom Trbojevic’s return would give the team a confidence boost. “He’s a world-class player,” Saab said. “He’s had a tough run with injuries this year, but whenever he’s been fit and played the full game, he’s always had an impact.



“We’re a better team when the Trbojevics are playing.” ‘Proud day for NRL’: Storm valued at $150m after sale goes through Adrian Proszenko The Melbourne Storm has been valued at more than $150 million after the world’s second-biggest investment firm bought a majority share of the club. After an exhaustive process to find the right partner, the Storm has completed a landmark transaction with EQT, a Swedish firm with more than $333 billion in assets under management.



Sualauvi Fa’alogo celebrates a try for Melbourne. Getty Images The sale puts the Storm alongside Collingwood and the Brisbane Broncos as one of Australia’s top sporting franchises, just after the NRL brokered a $5.3 billion broadcast deal. Storm chair Matt Tripp – who remains a co-owner alongside Bart Campbell, Gerry Ryan, Tom Carroll and Brett Ralph – said the deal will elevate one of Australia’s top-performing sports clubs even higher. “I’m really proud that a firm like EQT, who are a serious blue-chip investment company, has chosen us as the team in Australia that they want to invest in,” Tripp said. “That’s a credit to our people and the work that’s gone on over the last 27 years and the 13 years I’ve been involved as a club.



“I’ve watched people work tirelessly at the Storm. Off the back of that, EQT recognised that and wanted to be part of that. It’s a really proud day for the club and the NRL more broadly. I think the NRL should be happy that a club has attracted the attention of a company like EQT.” The deal, which will result in EQT earning board seats, is subject to Australian Rugby League Commission approval. Tripp will remain chair, while other key positions will remain the same. “Absolutely status quo,” Tripp said. “I’m still the largest shareholder after EQT and I’m as committed as I’ve ever been. It wouldn’t matter if I owned one per cent of 100 per cent, I’m still as passionate and my desire to drive this club doesn’t waiver … “These guys own the IMG Academy, which will be really beneficial for us. “It’s one of the biggest academies in the world, they effectively groom and produce through their pathways academy in the US the best of the best in gridiron, basketball, baseball and the like. “In terms of sports science and everything that goes on that is best in class, we feel we can benefit from that and our new partners will assist us. “They are also huge investors in the AI space and data and hopefully some of that can be transformed into improving areas of the club.” No Red V lifeline as Sloan seeks Super League answers Dan Walsh



Dragons flyer Tyrell Sloan says he has been “left in the dark” about the future of Castleford coach Ryan Carr, as St George Illawarra rule out extending an NRL lifeline to him and teammates Damien Cook and Mat Feagai if they look to back out of their Super League deals. Sloan conceded after the Dragons’ two-point win over Wests Tigers on Sunday that he has had second thoughts about his move to Castleford given the uncertainty around Carr’s position. Carr was a key reason Sloan signed a two-year deal with the club last month. Carr, who coached Sloan as an assistant and interim head coach at the Dragons, has been absent from Castleford for the past two weeks after the club launched an investigation into the 38-year-old with little detail or public explanation as to why. Castleford head of football Chris Chester has spoken to the Dragons trio and told them they remain in the club’s plans for next season regardless of Carr’s situation. Loading



St George Illawarra have moved on in their roster planning for 2027 and have privately conveyed that they do not have room for Sloan, Cook and Feagai in their salary cap after a significant recruitment and retention spree. “It definitely puts a big dent in things for me, I’ll be honest,” Sloan said. “Carry was a big reason why I signed over there. “Obviously we had a relationship here at the Dragons and I don’t really know the situation with him. We’ve been left in the dark. “I’m really excited to go over there if Carry is there, but I just don’t know if that’s going to be the case there. Hopefully I’ll find out soon what’s going on and they make a decision. Dragons flyer Tyrell Sloan. Getty Images



“I have thought about [trying to stay in the NRL], but I also have to keep playing good footy here to finish the season on a high.” Sloan, 24, has been playing with a new lease on life since Dean Young took charge of the Dragons, scoring eight tries in his past eight games. Immortal Andrew Johns has argued Sloan is “too good a player to be leaving the NRL at this age”, but the Indigenous All Stars representative acknowledged his form in previous years hadn’t left him with many options. “I didn’t really have much [many options] in the NRL, and nothing really made sense, you know, to play in another jersey in the NRL,” Sloan said. “But Joey’s always been really good to me since I came into first grade and to be getting a fair rap from someone who has done everything in the game, I hold that in such respect. World.title: CBA punishes Qantas customers in reward points overhaul
World.content:
Commonwealth Bank is pushing customers to spend their credit card rewards with Virgin’s Velocity scheme instead of Qantas Frequent Flyer points, as part of a dramatic overhaul of its loyalty program. Under the scheme unveiled on Tuesday, customers wanting to convert points earned under the bank’s new “Yello” scheme to airline rewards will get more generous rates when cashing them in with Virgin’s Velocity program rather than Qantas Frequent Flyer. The Commonwealth Bank is cutting back the generosity of its points schemes. Renee Nowytarger The move has been driven by the Reserve Bank of Australia’s decision to ban, from October 1, credit card surcharges that had funded credit card perks. This also pushed Westpac to announce fee hikes and cuts to benefits such as free travel insurance on its credit card line-up on Monday. Announcing the Yello-Virgin partnership, CBA would not reveal details of how many Yello points will be needed to redeem Virgin, Qantas and other brand loyalty points. Customers will only learn of their diminished Qantas points earning potential closer to the scheme’s effective date, also October 1.



Among the changes, Commbank customers who bundle multiple products, such as a mortgage or term deposits, with the bank will earn more points than those who have one account. The bank hopes that encouraging customer loyalty will help pay for the scheme, as the sector grapples with a shortfall in revenue from card fees. Related Article Exclusive

Loyalty programs Credit card rewards points slashed up to 50% ahead of surcharge ban Angus Sullivan, head of the bank’s retail division, said the change would enable more customers to earn rewards. “For the first time, more than nine million of our customers can earn points on the everyday banking they’re already doing – their home loan, savings, insurance and cards – and redeem them on the things that matter, from groceries, utility bills and fuel through to a well-earned holiday,” Sullivan said. The Reserve Bank’s reforms include the surcharge ban and a cap on fees paid by merchants every time a shopper pays for something with a card, which is expected to cut banks’ revenue by $660 million a year.



On Monday, Westpac unveiled a tightening of its credit card program, including cutting complimentary travel insurance from October and hiking annual fees, cash advance and interest rates, while keeping points earning rates relatively stable. In a similar move, NAB announced last month that it would cut the points earning rates on some of the cards it provides for other brands, including Bank of Queensland and Virgin Money, by up to 50 per cent. From September 30, some of NAB’s own credit cards will have their points earning rates reduced by about a third. Sources with knowledge of the Commonwealth Bank’s new scheme said Virgin offered the bank a better deal on Velocity points than Qantas did for Frequent Flyer points. Among other retailers, CBA has partnered with DoorDash, Woolworths, Origin Energy and Myer. Following CBA’s announcement, Qantas said it was still discussing participation in the Yello program, and noted anyone who has already set up their Commbank credit card to earn Frequent Flier points could keep transferring points.



Rewards advice website The Champagne Mile publisher Adele Eliseo said CBA’s move to focus on its own rewards program was a move to stamp out opportunistic credit card churners taking advantage of generous sign-on bonuses by switching banks. “This is very much designed to promote stickiness to more intensely align customers with the bank,” she said, adding that the model was popular in the US. Velocity points may be easier to earn, but Point Hacks spokesman Daniel Sciberras said he does not expect the points difference between Qantas and Virgin to push rusted-on Frequent Flier point collectors away from CBA. “But if you’re an optimiser and you’re just looking at just what the transfer rate is, maybe this will sway you towards Velocity,” Sciberras said. Virgin Velocity chief executive Andrew Cleary believed the simplicity of the new CBA scheme would increase its uptake. It was a sign the bank was running its “own race”.

World.title: ICAC Operation Rosny LIVE updates: Former Perrottet government minister Eleni Petinos to appear
World.content:
Hello and welcome to another day of the ICAC’s Operation Rosny live hearings.

I’m state political reporter Jessica McSweeney and along with the Herald’s team of senior writers, we’ll be bringing you all the news as it happens from inside the hearing.

Today we’re hearing evidence from former fair trading minister Eleni Petinos and her former chief of staff Cassandra Lawry. Before then, let’s take a look at what we covered yesterday:

Dallas McInerney wiped his phone and iPad with a factory reset the weekend before returning the devices to Catholic Schools NSW, he says, after his bank alerted him to an issue with security on his bank account. Counsel assisting Peggy Dwyer, SC, suggested it was a “transparent attempt to wipe evidence”, which McInerney denied.

McInerney said he handed his devices back to Catholic Schools NSW because he understood it was unlikely he would be returning to work.

Dwyer said investigators had struggled to find any substantive documentation of work done by Beckington or JPG Advisory, which the ICAC is investigating in connection with allegations Catholic Schools NSW money was funnelled into the pockets of Liberal Party factional operators. McInerney said most of the work was done in meetings or over the phone, which was “safer”.

McInerney discussed Liberal Party matters and his own political ambitions with Jeremy Greenwood, who ran JPG Advisory.

McInerney sent a draft position description and negotiated with Jean-Claude Perrottet about a job at Catholic Schools NSW, at least partly while Perrottet was avoiding a parliamentary inquiry by travelling to Fiji.

World.title: ‘Decisions soon’: KPMG starts talks on staff purge
World.content:
Updated BusinessCompaniesConsulting ‘Decisions soon’: KPMG starts talks on staff purge Colin Kruger Updated August 20, 2026 — 9:01am ,first published 8:00am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

KPMG chief executive John Sams confirmed that the embattled firm has begun talks with senior partners who will be cut as part of a massive staff purge expected next week due to the whistleblower scandal engulfing the firm. “I have been clear in recent communications with partners and our people that we are undertaking a process to review our cost base and workforce to ensure the firm is sustainable and well positioned for the future,” he told partners in an email on Wednesday evening. No decisions have been made about staff roles at this point but, as I have said in previous communications, we expect to make those decisions soon.“: KPMG Australia CEO John Sams sent an email to staff on Wednesday night. Alex Ellinghausen “Conversations have commenced this week with impacted partners. No decisions have been made about staff roles at this point but, as I have said in previous communications, we expect to make those decisions soon.” Sams said he expects to provide a further update next week.



Internal sources have said this is when the firm is expected to announce as many as 1000 staff will be cut in response to the massive change of fortunes since KPMG confirmed whistleblower allegations that confidential customer information was used to try and win new audit business. The planned job cuts come just one week after current and former KPMG executives were forced to front another public hearing into the scandal. Renee Nowytarger The Australian reported 500 staff will be cut, which is at the lower end of estimates in recent weeks. “I am frustrated and sorry that we are all dealing with this speculation. I know it is unsettling for all of us, and our teams,” Sams said. “I can’t comment any further until decisions are made but I expect to provide a further update next week.”



The planned job cuts come just one week after current and former KPMG executives were forced to front another public hearing into the scandal. Sacked KPMG executive Eileen Hoggett was confronted with evidence showing she emailed a colleague about confidential documents stored in her locker. Hoggett told the hearing she was still trying to ascertain the reason for her unprecedented sacking, and attested to the financial cost. “I don’t get my accrued annual leave. I don’t get the retirement payment, which I contributed to as a partner for 21 years, and I did not get paid for the last month up until to the date of my expulsion. So (it’s a) significant financial penalty,” she said. This week, the Australian Securities and Investments Commission’s (ASIC) revealed its probe into the whistleblower scandal at KPMG now includes companies controlled by the accounting and consulting giant, and potentially these companies’ directors.

World.title: Wong outraged as Israel clears soldiers over strike that killed Australian Zomi Frankcom
World.content:
Israel’s ambassador to Australia has been summoned for a rebuke after the country cleared its military of any criminal wrongdoing over an attack in Gaza that killed seven aid workers, including Australian Zomi Frankcom. The Israeli Defence Forces (IDF) decided there was “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct” in the strike on the World Central Kitchen (WCK) workers in April 2024 as they delivered humanitarian aid to a warehouse. Australian Zomi Frankcom was killed in a 2024 airstrike while delivering aid in Gaza with World Central Kitchen. The formal IDF decision came hours after Foreign Minister Penny Wong called for “full accountability” over the deaths, as she honoured Frankcom at an event in Canberra on Wednesday to launch a humanitarian award in her name. Wong released a strongly worded statement on Thursday morning, expressing Australia’s outrage and pointing out she learnt of Israel’s decision on World Humanitarian Day moments before it was announced – a fact that was “especially insulting to Zomi’s loved ones, humanitarians and all Australians”.



“This decision falls far short of the accountability we expect,” Wong said. “Democracies seek and accept higher standards. The Australian government will not stop pressing Israel for justice for Zomi and her colleagues.” The foreign minister added that she will call in Israel’s ambassador – a process where a diplomat is summoned for a formal warning or dressing down – and that Australia was considering its next steps. The outcome was one of five IDF reports issued on Wednesday into separate incidents. In one case, which made global headlines, five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab died in January 2024 after pleading to be rescued from an attack that had killed her aunt, uncle and three cousins. Hind Rajab, who was killed alongside her family in an Israeli strike in 2024. Family Handout via AP



The IDF ruled there should be a criminal investigation by the military police into the death of Rajab, her family members, as well as paramedics who sought to come to her aid. In a second case, the IDF decided there should also be a criminal investigation into an ambush by Israeli forces that killed 15 Palestinians, including medical personnel, as well as a United Nations employee in March 2025. The decision on Frankcom and her colleagues outraged WCK, which condemned the outcome and called for an independent inquiry into the airstrikes on the grounds that the Israeli military could not credibly investigate its own conduct. Frankcom, 43, and six colleagues died on April 1, 2024 when the vehicle they were travelling in was fired upon while delivering aid in Gaza. The IDF said its officers had “mistakenly believed that the vehicles contained Hamas military operatives and therefore struck the vehicles”.



It claimed that attempts were made to contact WCK representatives during “the approximately half-hour period in which the convoy vehicles were tracked on the understanding that they contained Hamas operatives”, but those attempts were unsuccessful. Related Article Israeli-Palestinian conflict ‘We have expressed sympathy’: Israeli ambassador declines to apologise for Zomi Frankcom killing The Israeli military said the presence of armed security to accompany the convoy “was not coordinated with IDF authorities” and the vehicles had deviated from the route arranged in advance, while several people were also mistakenly identified as armed persons. “Following review of all findings of the factual assessment, it was determined that, notwithstanding serious failures in the process that led to the assessment that Hamas operatives were travelling in the vehicles, the decisions of the commanders did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct,” the IDF said. It added that there was “no reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct that would justify the opening of a criminal investigation”.



Two Israeli officers were dismissed from their positions and three senior officers were formally reprimanded, according to the Israeli military. WCK said it fundamentally disagreed with the decision not to pursue a criminal investigation. “We strongly condemn the Israeli military prosecutor’s account of the deaths of our seven colleagues on April 1, 2024,” the aid organisation said in a statement. “There has never been any excuse or justification for the attacks, and there is nothing in this account that does so. The decision is inconsistent with the full truth and deeply offensive.” Wong spoke in Canberra on Wednesday at a Parliament House event attended by Frankcom’s family to launch the Zomi Frankcom Humanitarian Award.



“Two years on from Zomi Frankcom’s death, the pain of her loss remains with us,” she said. “People like Zomi are rare, and their courage deserves to be celebrated. “I want to make it clear that the Australian government continues to press the Israeli government for full accountability for the deaths of Zomi and her World Central Kitchen colleagues. Zomi and her family deserve justice.” Foreign Minister Penny Wong with Zomi Frankcom’s brother, Mal Frankcom, in September 2025. Dominic Lorrimer In a report released in July 2024, former Australian Defence Force chief Mark Binskin found that “a significant breakdown in situational awareness” by the Israeli military caused the strike that killed Frankcom, adding he did not believe the charity workers were deliberately targeted.



The IDF said its Fact-Finding and Assessment Mechanism (FFAM) had reviewed approximately 150 incidents since the beginning of the war, then transferred them for examination by the Military Prosecution. Related Article Israeli-Palestinian conflict Netanyahu bluntly rejects Trump’s Gaza plan to disarm Hamas Rajab and her family were trapped in a vehicle under fire in Gaza City in January 2024, while she pleaded for help by phone with her cousin Layan Hamada beside her. The IDF concluded that in the hours shortly after the firing, following a telephone call to rescue authorities, the movement of a Palestine Red Crescent ambulance was coordinated for the purpose of evacuating the casualties. “However, according to the allegations raised, upon the ambulance’s arrival at the scene of the incident, a shell was fired toward it, resulting in the deaths of the two paramedics travelling in it,” the IDF said.



“Several days later, the bodies of the seven members of the Hamada family, including the bodies of Hind and Layan, were recovered from the vehicle. In addition, the bodies of the two paramedics were recovered from the ambulance. “It has been decided to initiate a criminal investigation of the incident by Military Police Criminal Investigation Division (MPCID). In light of this decision, no further details can be provided beyond the above with respect to the aspects arising from the FFAM’s review.” The 15 Palestinian paramedics were killed as they drove in the southern city of Rafah in March 2025. The IDF decided not to take criminal action over the killings of four staffers from Doctors Without Borders in two separate instances in November 2023 and February 2024. On Wednesday, an Israeli airstrike killed nine Palestinians at a police station in Gaza, medics said.



Medics and police sources said several officers were among those killed at what the Hamas-led interior ministry said was the headquarters of the municipal police. Fifteen others were wounded. The Israeli military said it had struck Hamas militants who “operated from the civilian police station” to advance attacks against its troops. Alan Jones arrives at the Downing Centre Local Court on Wednesday. Peter Rae

Latrell Mitchell at South Sydney training earlier this week. Steven Siewert But Souths have opted to keep their superstar centre on ice for another week. Tom Trbojevic is a huge addition to a Manly side that remains a mathematical possibility of squeaking into the finals if they beat Newcastle at McDonald Jones Stadium on Saturday.

Related Article Opinion

NRL 2026 Twelve months ago, the Knights were heading for the wooden spoon. Holbrook must be coach of the year Malcolm Knox Journalist, author and columnist



“I didn’t really have much [many options] in the NRL, and nothing really made sense, you know, to play in another jersey in the NRL,” Sloan said. “But Joey’s always been really good to me since I came into first grade and to be getting a fair rap from someone who has done everything in the game, I hold that in such respect. At the moment, I’ve got the Super League deal and at the end of it, I’ll only be 26. I’ve been in first grade since I was 18 so no matter what happens, I’d say I’ve got a lot of NRL left in me.”

World.title: CBA punishes Qantas customers in reward points overhaul
World.content:
Commonwealth Bank is pushing customers to spend their credit card rewards with Virgin’s Velocity scheme instead of Qantas Frequent Flyer points, as part of a dramatic overhaul of its loyalty program. Under the scheme unveiled on Tuesday, customers wanting to convert points earned under the bank’s new “Yello” scheme to airline rewards will get more generous rates when cashing them in with Virgin’s Velocity program rather than Qantas Frequent Flyer. The Commonwealth Bank is cutting back the generosity of its points schemes. Renee Nowytarger The move has been driven by the Reserve Bank of Australia’s decision to ban, from October 1, credit card surcharges that had funded credit card perks. This also pushed Westpac to announce fee hikes and cuts to benefits such as free travel insurance on its credit card line-up on Monday. Announcing the Yello-Virgin partnership, CBA would not reveal details of how many Yello points will be needed to redeem Virgin, Qantas and other brand loyalty points. Customers will only learn of their diminished Qantas points earning potential closer to the scheme’s effective date, also October 1.



Among the changes, Commbank customers who bundle multiple products, such as a mortgage or term deposits, with the bank will earn more points than those who have one account. The bank hopes that encouraging customer loyalty will help pay for the scheme, as the sector grapples with a shortfall in revenue from card fees. Related Article Exclusive

Loyalty programs Credit card rewards points slashed up to 50% ahead of surcharge ban Angus Sullivan, head of the bank’s retail division, said the change would enable more customers to earn rewards. “For the first time, more than nine million of our customers can earn points on the everyday banking they’re already doing – their home loan, savings, insurance and cards – and redeem them on the things that matter, from groceries, utility bills and fuel through to a well-earned holiday,” Sullivan said. The Reserve Bank’s reforms include the surcharge ban and a cap on fees paid by merchants every time a shopper pays for something with a card, which is expected to cut banks’ revenue by $660 million a year.



On Monday, Westpac unveiled a tightening of its credit card program, including cutting complimentary travel insurance from October and hiking annual fees, cash advance and interest rates, while keeping points earning rates relatively stable. In a similar move, NAB announced last month that it would cut the points earning rates on some of the cards it provides for other brands, including Bank of Queensland and Virgin Money, by up to 50 per cent. From September 30, some of NAB’s own credit cards will have their points earning rates reduced by about a third. Sources with knowledge of the Commonwealth Bank’s new scheme said Virgin offered the bank a better deal on Velocity points than Qantas did for Frequent Flyer points. Among other retailers, CBA has partnered with DoorDash, Woolworths, Origin Energy and Myer. Following CBA’s announcement, Qantas said it was still discussing participation in the Yello program, and noted anyone who has already set up their Commbank credit card to earn Frequent Flier points could keep transferring points.



Rewards advice website The Champagne Mile publisher Adele Eliseo said CBA’s move to focus on its own rewards program was a move to stamp out opportunistic credit card churners taking advantage of generous sign-on bonuses by switching banks. “This is very much designed to promote stickiness to more intensely align customers with the bank,” she said, adding that the model was popular in the US. Velocity points may be easier to earn, but Point Hacks spokesman Daniel Sciberras said he does not expect the points difference between Qantas and Virgin to push rusted-on Frequent Flier point collectors away from CBA. “But if you’re an optimiser and you’re just looking at just what the transfer rate is, maybe this will sway you towards Velocity,” Sciberras said. Virgin Velocity chief executive Andrew Cleary believed the simplicity of the new CBA scheme would increase its uptake. It was a sign the bank was running its “own race”.

World.title: WA news LIVE: Perth father hospitalised in Bali after ‘brutal’ group attack
World.content:
A Perth father is in intensive care at a Bali hospital after being attacked by a “group of Australians” while on holiday at the popular Indonesian tourist island.

Liam Dougan has started a fundraiser for his father, Paul, who has undergone three surgeries, including to have his spleen removed, after the attack.

Perth father Paul Dougan has been hospitalised in Bali after allegedly being assaulted by fellow Australians while on holiday. GoFundMe
